positions.commentary: The speaker mentions IBM as an example of a company whose value is determined by active investors like Howard Marks and Monash.
Tesla is harder to see as a quality company, more speculative lately, and the speaker is not comfortable calling it a quality company due to uncertainties.
Amazon is a quality company that took a long time to prove and realize value, requiring a long hold through thick and thin.
Unilever is a quality business that needs to navigate different cycles and maintain solid economic performance, sometimes stronger, sometimes weaker.

thesis: This episode argues that investors should focus on 'quality' companies that have proven their value over time, even if it requires a long hold through various market cycles. It contrasts established quality businesses like Amazon and Unilever with more speculative firms like Tesla, suggesting that true quality investing involves navigating economic uncertainty while maintaining solid performance.
